title: gc: empty boot_id classifies every project as Orphan, so 'pctl gc --yes' purges all of them
description:
Pre-existing (not introduced by the dead-code-cleanup diff, which only renamed the reader).

lib/gc/gc.ml:97,118,139 read the boot id via Clock.Real.read_boot_id, which degrades to "" on any read failure (lib/clock/clock.ml:44).

lib/gc/gc.ml:32-37:
    match row.session_id with
    | Some s when s = boot_id && s <> "" -> Schema.Live
    | _ -> Schema.Orphan

With boot_id = "" the guard can never hold: s = boot_id forces s = "", which the s <> "" clause then rejects. Every row with an existing path becomes Orphan. Gc.purge (gc.ml:117-133) removes every Orphan, so 'pctl gc --yes' deletes the whole registry — units stopped, unit files removed, rows dropped — whenever /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id is unreadable.

Before the diff this was Gc.current_boot_id = try State.Session.read_boot_id () with _ -> "" — same degrade, same hazard.

Fix: route all three gc sites through Clock.read_boot_id_exn, which propagates instead. Gc.opportunistic_sweep already wraps its body in a warn-and-proceed try, so a raise there degrades to a skipped sweep rather than an aborted command; purge and report should fail loudly.

Note the comment added at lib/clock/clock.ml:11-16 asserts the opposite — that State.Session.reset is the *single* caller that must not get "".

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Fixed in the working tree (uncommitted; awaiting commit sha to close).

lib/gc/gc.ml:97,118,139 now read via Clock.read_boot_id_exn instead of the degrading Clock.Real.read_boot_id, so an unreadable boot id refuses to classify rather than reclassifying every project as Orphan.

lib/clock/clock.ml: read_boot_id_exn additionally raises Sys_error (path ^ ": empty boot id") when the trimmed read is empty — the reviewer's second finding. A zero-byte or whitespace-only read previously returned the exact "" the function existed to prevent, so routing gc through it would not have sufficed alone.

The false 'single caller' comment is replaced by the real hazard list (Session.reset AND Gc.class_of_row).

Blast radius: opportunistic_sweep already wraps its body in warn-and-proceed, so it degrades to a skipped sweep; purge and report now fail loudly instead of deleting rows. Clock.Real.read_boot_id survives with exactly one caller — Pipeline.with_project's metadata stamp, where "" legitimately means NULL session_id.

Regression cover: test/unit/test_clock.ml (new) pins all four leak paths — trims a good read, raises on blank/zero-byte/missing.

Gates: dune test exit 0 (incl. 4 new cases); dune build @e2e --force exit 0, all 22 scenarios OK against a live user session; nix build .#pctl exit 0.

title: probe: a missing probe executable aborts the wait instead of being retried as a failed probe
description:
Pre-existing. Adjacent to this diff because the diff deletes Schema.Probe_exec_failed as dead code — the constructor that named exactly this case.

lib/probe/probe.ml:112-115 states:

  (* Run the probe command ONCE; return true iff exit-0. Any spawn error
   * (executable not found, ...) is treated as false — matches the
   * Nushell 'probe-once' behaviour, which keeps the wait alive long
   * enough for a slow-to-appear readiness flag file to materialise. *)

run_probe_once (lib/probe/probe.ml:120-136) has no try/with. Eio 1.3 declares

  type error = Executable_not_found of string | Child_error of exit_status

in eio/process.mli, and Eio.Process.await returns only exit_status ('Exited | 'Signaled), so Executable_not_found can only reach the caller as a raised Eio.Exn.Io. It therefore escapes run_probe_once and tears down the wait instead of yielding false and retrying.

Fix: wrap the spawn/await in

  try ... with Eio.Exn.Io _ -> false

and decide deliberately whether a permanently-missing executable should still burn the full probe timeout, or fail fast with a distinct error. If the latter, Probe_exec_failed (deleted in the cleanup diff) is the shape to restore.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Review of the pctl-lrc working tree: the code comment that documents the non-existent swallow is still in the tree, and the same diff now adds a plan-doc note asserting the opposite, so the two contradict each other.

lib/probe/probe.ml:112-115:

  (* Run the probe command ONCE; return true iff exit-0. Any spawn error
   * (executable not found, ...) is treated as false — matches the
   * Nushell `probe-once` behaviour, which keeps the wait alive long
   * enough for a slow-to-appear readiness flag file to materialise. *)

run_probe_once (probe.ml:120-136) has no try/with — re-confirmed by reading it. Meanwhile docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md:49-54, added by that diff, states plainly that 'Probe.run_probe_once does not catch the Eio.Exn.Io that a missing probe executable raises'.

Correcting the comment is a one-liner and does not need this ticket's behavioural decision: say that the spawn error currently escapes and that pctl-j9k owns whether it should be retried as false or fail fast. Flagged in the review as an optional in-scope fix.

Separately, probe.ml:123-126 returns false for an empty exec list with the justification 'the Spec loader should have caught this. Defensive'. Whoever restores the error path should confirm the Spec loader actually rejects an empty probe exec; if it does not, that is a second unconstructed error path in the same function.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Comment at lib/probe/probe.ml:112-121 corrected to state the actual behaviour and point here — it previously claimed 'Any spawn error (executable not found, ...) is treated as false', which contradicted both the code and the note added at docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md. Behaviour deliberately unchanged; this issue still owns the fix and the timeout-vs-fail-fast decision.

title: review: dead-code cleanup diff (pre-v0.1.0 working tree)
description: Holds the review report for the uncommitted 'simplify code and delete dead code' working tree on top of 0508423. See the report comment.
close_reason: Completed: commit:63111ca52cc812bab91aa4325957b870face2ba7 commit:c7fb526033426ca04d980417e2d4b0d2419668d8 — all report items fixed; residue re-filed and linked via discovered-from (pctl-2jn closed; pctl-j9k, pctl-oik, pctl-4qh, pctl-79a, pctl-jbd open)

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
## Review — uncommitted tree vs. intent "simplify code and delete dead code"

Scope: 24 modified files, no untracked files. Gates run this session: `dune test` → exit 0; `dune build @e2e --force` → exit 0 against the live user session (`systemctl --user is-system-running` → degraded, i.e. running).

### Silent failures / implicit values

- `lib/clock/clock.ml:11-16` — the new comment claims "the single caller who must NOT get '' is [State.Session.reset]". False: `Gc.class_of_row` (gc.ml:32-37) treats "" as matching nothing, so an empty boot id makes every project Orphan and `Gc.purge` (gc.ml:117-133, on `Clock.Real.read_boot_id`) deletes the entire registry. Fix: route gc's three sites through `Clock.read_boot_id_exn`, and drop the "single caller" claim. Behaviour is unchanged from before the diff (old `Gc.current_boot_id` degraded identically) — the false invariant is what this diff adds. Hazard tracked as pctl-2jn.
- `lib/clock/clock.ml:17-28` — `read_boot_id_exn` raises only on open/read failure; a zero-byte or whitespace `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` still returns "", the exact value the comment says the raising variant exists to prevent. Fix: after `String.trim`, raise `Sys_error (boot_id_path ^ ": empty boot id")` when the result is empty.

### Standards / docs consistency

- `docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md:270` — still lists `Probe_exec_failed of { service : string; msg : string }` in the error sketch, which this diff deletes from `lib/schema/schema.ml`. The diff updates four other stale comments for exactly this reason (CLAUDE.md layout line, bin/pctl.ml, lib/cli/dune, nix/lib/default.nix); this one was missed. Fix: delete the line or add a follow-up note in the doc's existing drift-note style.
- `lib/cli/init.ml:131-137` — the new guard fixes the case where no template `.gitignore` exists, but when one exists and `needed = []` (lines 113-127 write nothing) it still prints "pctl init: updated <path>". Same truthfulness gap the guard was added to close, one level deeper. Fix: hoist a `wrote_gitignore` bool out of the merge branch and gate the print on it.

### Intent

The diff is a faithful dead-code deletion — every removed API (`Project_id.compare`, `Host.compare`, `Project_path.of_raw_opt/equal/compare`, `Projects.get_by_path`, `Probe_exec_failed`, `Lifecycle.report.manifest_before/after`, `Harness.assert_dropin_exists`, `sd_bus_get_fd`, `Dbus.t.env`, the `logs` opam dep) verified unreferenced, and the three dedups (`Plan.sort_rows`, `Probe.error_of_row`, `Clock` boot-id reader) collapse genuine duplicates.

One change exceeds "delete dead code" and is worth naming: moving `sd_bus_call_method_*` and `sd_bus_message_read_*` from top-level `let … = foreign …` into the lazily-built `Ffi.t` record (dbus.ml:126-256) is a behaviour fix, not a cleanup. `foreign` calls `libsystemd ()` (dbus.ml:53-56), which raises `Bus_connect_failed` when dlopen fails, so the old top-level bindings ran dlopen at module-initialisation time — defeating the laziness the module header claims at dbus.ml:3-5. Correct change; it just isn't dead-code removal.

### Discarded on verification

- `Probe_failed` → `Probe_timeout` is not a mislabel: probe.ml:279-283 sets `Probe_failed` when the per-service deadline fires before the overall one, so both branches are genuine timeouts.
- `Probe.error_of_row` vs. the deleted `Pipeline.error_of_row`: the `Active` branch differs, but `worst_row` (pipeline.ml:62-77) never returns an `Active` row, so the old branch was unreachable. No behaviour change.
- `let _ = message_exit_container` discards in dbus.ml: unchanged by this diff and unreachable after a successful enter+read.

### Pre-existing, filed

pctl-2jn (gc purges everything on an empty boot id), pctl-j9k (a missing probe executable aborts the wait; `Probe_exec_failed`, deleted here, was its constructor).

### Verdict

Not blocking, but four small fixes are worth taking before `/commit`: the two `clock.ml` items, the stale plan-doc line, and the `init.ml` print. Note `.beads/` was created during this review and must be staged (or gitignored) deliberately — flakes evaluate the git tree, so it is currently invisible to `nix flake check`.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Took all four fixes from the review. Verified each claim against the code first; all four held.

1. lib/clock/clock.ml false 'single caller' comment — confirmed. class_of_row guards Live on 's = boot_id && s <> ""', which "" cannot satisfy, so gc --yes would delete the registry. Comment now lists both hazards; gc's three sites routed through Clock.read_boot_id_exn (see pctl-2jn).
2. read_boot_id_exn returning "" for a blank read — confirmed. Now raises Sys_error (path ^ ": empty boot id"). Added an injectable ?path (test-only) so the invariant is testable, plus test/unit/test_clock.ml covering trim / blank / zero-byte / missing.
3. docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md:270 — Probe_exec_failed line removed, replaced by a short note that it was never constructed and that pctl-j9k owns reinstating it. Keeps the deferred intent discoverable from the plan.
4. lib/cli/init.ml 'updated <path>' when needed = [] — confirmed. Hoisted a wrote_gitignore ref out of the merge branch; the line now fires only on an actual write.

On the intent note: agreed, the Ffi.t move is a behaviour fix, not dead-code removal. Worth recording that its user-visible blast radius is nil — (c_library_flags (-lsystemd)) puts libsystemd in every executable's DT_NEEDED (ldd on test_schema.exe confirms it resolves at process start), so the module-init dlopen could never actually have failed. The change makes the header's laziness claim true and collapses two FFI declaration mechanisms into one.

Also correcting my own earlier justification for deleting Probe_exec_failed: I wrote that run_probe_once 'deliberately swallows spawn errors', which was me repeating its comment rather than reading it. There is no try/with — pctl-j9k is right. The variant was still unconstructible, so the deletion stands, but the reason is 'the error path was never wired', not 'errors are swallowed'.

Gates: dune test exit 0; dune build @e2e --force exit 0 (22/22 against a live session, is-system-running = degraded); nix build .#pctl exit 0.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
## Re-review — working tree after the four fixes + pctl-2jn

Gates run this session, on the host with a live user session (`systemctl --user is-system-running` → degraded):
- `dune test` → exit 0.
- `dune build @e2e --force` → **exit 1 on the first run**, exit 0 on runs 2 and 3. Run 1 failed in test_pctl_no_gc at `up(a)`: `systemctl Reload - failed: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply: Remote peer disconnected`. The test passes 6/6 solo. Filed as pctl-jbd. The prior comment's claim of "exit 0, all 22 scenarios OK" does not reproduce reliably — the gate is ~2/3.
- `nix build .#pctl` not run this session.

All four prescribed fixes and pctl-2jn's three gc sites verified present and correct. What follows is what the fixes left behind.

### Stale comments the fix pass missed

- `test/unit/test_gc.ml:143` — "if current_boot_id () returns \"\"" names the function this diff deletes. Fix: say `boot_id = ""`.
- `lib/probe/probe.ml:112-115` — "Any spawn error (executable not found, ...) is treated as false" is false; `run_probe_once` (120-136) has no `try/with`, and the plan-doc note this diff *adds* (docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md:49-54) says so explicitly. The tree now contradicts itself. Fix: one line saying the spawn error currently escapes, ref pctl-j9k. Commented there.
- `UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:21` — links `lib/install/`, deleted (`ls lib/` has no `install`). `UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:89` — Harness row lists `write-tree` and `cleanup-stragglers`; neither exists in test/e2e/harness.ml. This diff fixed the identical `cleanup_stragglers` claim at CLAUDE.md:33 and missed its twin, in the file CLAUDE.md mandates reading before writing code or docs.

### Dead assertion

- `test/unit/test_gc.ml:229-249` — `test_purge_preserves_live_rows` reads the *degrading* `Clock.Real.read_boot_id` while `G.purge` now reads `read_boot_id_exn` (gc.ml:126). The `else` branch asserting "empty boot_id → both removed" is unreachable and states the pre-fix contract: with an unreadable boot id, line 239's `G.purge` raises `Sys_error` before returning, so the test errors rather than degrading. Fix: `let boot = Clock.read_boot_id_exn () in`, delete the `if boot <> ""` split and the comment above it.

### Reuse

- `lib/clock/clock.ml:31-37` — the byte-at-a-time `Buffer.add_channel buf ic 1` loop reimplements `In_channel.input_all`, which handles exactly the virtual-file case the comment cites. Verified directly on OCaml 5.4.1: on `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, `in_channel_length` = 0 while `In_channel.input_all` returns all 37 bytes. `dune-project:8` requires `(ocaml (>= 5.0))`. Fix: `String.trim (In_channel.input_all ic)`; the comment then only has to explain the trim and the empty check, not the drain.

### Filed rather than fixed here

pctl-4qh (`Session.reset` bypasses the Clock port, so `Clock.frozen ~boot:"test-boot"` in test/integration/test_pipeline_up.ml:25 does not freeze the boot id that decides row deletion; also why pipeline.ml:192's `if boot_id = "" then None` is now a dead branch encoding a false invariant, and why lib/state gained a `clock` dep), pctl-79a (the new `Sys_error` renders as `pctl: unexpected error: …` exit 1 via pipeline.ml:55-57, outside the exit-code taxonomy at schema.ml:486-497), pctl-jbd (the e2e flake above).

Pre-existing: pctl-8sd (lifecycle.ml:162-163 tear-down swallows the slice `stop_unit` failure, then unloads the slice and deletes every unit file — live processes left in an unmanaged cgroup; the header's tolerance justification covers `Removed` rows in `apply_row`, not this site), pctl-lfu (dbus.ml:463-479 folds `sd_bus_process` rc < 0 into the idle branch and drops `sd_bus_wait`'s rc — a persistent bus error spins at 100ms forever and surfaces as a probe timeout), pctl-vz9 (dbus.ml:34-52 discards both `Dl.DL_error` messages, so a wrong-ELF or undefined-symbol libsystemd reports "not found … check LD_LIBRARY_PATH"), pctl-6ra (gc.ml:111-115,118-120 catch-alls swallow `Eio.Cancel.Cancelled`, so Ctrl-C during a sweep warns and the command continues), pctl-ntl (test_helpers.ml:32-38 `write_temp_file` never removes the file).

### Not findings, on verification

- The CRITICAL data-loss shape around `Clock.Real.read_boot_id` → NULL `session_id` → `Orphan` → `gc --yes` does **not** reach production: every path into `with_project` enters `with_connection` first (pipeline.ml:169 → 40-45), where `Session.reset` already raised on an unreadable or blank boot id. Reaching the destructive path needs the same /proc file to succeed and then fail microseconds later. What survives is the dead branch, filed as pctl-4qh.
- `Fun.protect` cannot wrap the empty-boot-id `Sys_error` as `Finally_raised` — the raise is outside the `protect` (clock.ml:39).
- `let _ = t.ffi.message_exit_container` — the diff only re-points the call; unreachable consequence after a successful enter+read.
- `with_boot_file` vs `Test_helpers.write_temp_file` — 5 lines, and the helper hardcodes a `.json` suffix that reads wrong for a boot-id fixture. Noted in pctl-ntl instead.
- `probe.ml:123-126` empty-`exec` → false — justification stated at the site.

### Untracked

`.beads/{.gitignore,config.yaml,issues.jsonl,metadata.json}` — still untracked, still not ignored (`git check-ignore` exits 1; root .gitignore has no `.beads` entry). The prior review flagged this and it was not acted on. `test/unit/test_clock.ml` *is* staged, so no build input is missing from the git tree and `nix flake check` is not false-greening on code — but committing without `git add .beads/` drops all nine tickets.

### Verdict

Not blocking. Five small fixes before `/commit`: the three stale comments, test_gc.ml's dead `else` branch, and the `In_channel.input_all` swap. Then `git add .beads/`. The e2e gate being ~2/3 reliable (pctl-jbd) is the one thing that should not be left implicit — it means neither this review nor the prior comment can honestly call e2e green from a single run.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text: Gate addendum: `nix flake check` → exit 0, all 6 checks passed (ocaml-tests, treefmt-check, statix, deadnix, …). Correcting the line above that said nix was not run this session — it now has been. `dune test` exit 0 and the e2e result (1 failure in 3 runs, pctl-jbd) stand as stated.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Second review pass — all five items verified against the code and fixed.

1. test/unit/test_gc.ml:143 — comment named the deleted current_boot_id (); now says boot_id = "" and notes class_of_row keeps the guard defensively even though Gc can no longer reach that state.
2. lib/probe/probe.ml:112-121 — comment rewritten to state that the catch was never written (Eio 1.3 raises Executable_not_found out of spawn; await only returns an exit status), tagged KNOWN BUG pctl-j9k. Tree no longer contradicts the plan-doc note. Behaviour untouched.
3. UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:21 (deleted lib/install/) and :89-91 (write-tree/cleanup-stragglers, scratch {tmp, project_dir, tree_dir}) fixed against test/e2e/harness.ml. Also fixed :62, the same class of error — it credited lib/plan/ with computing the diff, which lives in State.Projects.diff_manifest.
4. test/unit/test_gc.ml:229-249 dead assertion — confirmed unreachable (G.purge reads read_boot_id_exn, which raises before returning, so the else branch could never run and stated the pre-fix contract). Now reads read_boot_id_exn, split deleted, assertions unconditional.
5. lib/clock/clock.ml — byte-at-a-time loop replaced with In_channel.with_open_text path In_channel.input_all. Verified independently on OCaml 5.4.1: in_channel_length = 0 on /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, input_all returns 37 bytes; empty file returns "", so the non-empty check still does the work. dune-project pins ocaml >= 5.0, input_all is 4.14+. Net 12 lines to 2.

Filed pctl-oik (p1): the gc section of UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md (:50-58) describes a state-dir/known-marker design that does not exist, and inverts Orphan vs Unknown plus the 'only Orphan is deleted' and 'Unknown never deleted automatically' claims. Left unfixed on purpose — it is a domain-model rewrite, not a comment fix.

Gates this pass: dune test exit 0; nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.ocaml-tests exit 0 (new — confirms the stricter reader is sandbox-safe, i.e. the Nix sandbox does expose a readable non-empty boot id); dune build @e2e --force exit 0, 22/22 on a live session; nix build .#pctl exit 0.

title: lifecycle: tear-down swallows the slice stop_unit failure, then deletes every unit file
dbus: dispatch_loop ignores negative rc from sd_bus_process and sd_bus_wait, spinning silently
description:
Pre-existing; lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:463-479. This diff re-pointed both calls from top-level foreigns to t.ffi.* but did not change the rc handling.

      let rec drain () =
        let rc = t.ffi.sd_bus_process t.bus msg_p in
        if rc > 0 then (... drain ())
        else ()
      ...
        let _rc = t.ffi.sd_bus_wait t.bus timeout_us in
        ()

The comment two lines above states the contract the code then ignores:

      (* Non-blocking drain. sd_bus_process returns > 0 if a message was
       * processed, 0 if none, < 0 on error. We loop until it returns 0. *)

'if rc > 0 ... else ()' folds rc < 0 into the same branch as rc = 0, so a bus error is indistinguishable from an idle bus. sd_bus_wait's rc is bound to _rc and dropped. A persistent error (bus disconnected, ENOMEM) therefore makes the loop spin at one 100ms sd_bus_wait per iteration forever, with nothing on stderr and no exception to any waiting fiber — the probe/subscribe path just never sees another PropertiesChanged and times out with a misleading Probe_timeout.

Fix: branch on rc < 0 explicitly in drain, and check sd_bus_wait's rc. On a negative rc, set t.dispatch_stopped and raise (or record) a Bus_connect_failed naming the errno so the waiting fiber fails with the real cause instead of a timeout.

title: dbus: dlopen discards the Dl.DL_error message, reporting 'not found' for any load failure
description:
Pre-existing; lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:34-52.

  let libsystemd_lazy : Dl.library option Lazy.t =
    lazy
      (try Some (Dl.dlopen ~filename:"libsystemd.so.0" ~flags:[ Dl.RTLD_NOW ])
       with Dl.DL_error _ -> (
         try Some (Dl.dlopen ~filename:"libsystemd.so" ~flags:[ Dl.RTLD_NOW ])
         with Dl.DL_error _ -> None))

Both DL_error payloads are dropped, and the None case then reports one fixed message:

    msg = "libsystemd.so.0 not found via dlopen; check LD_LIBRARY_PATH or systemdLibs build input"

dlopen with RTLD_NOW fails for reasons other than absence: a wrong ELF class (32/64-bit mismatch), an undefined symbol in the library or its own dependencies, or a permission error. All of them surface as 'not found ... check LD_LIBRARY_PATH', which sends the reader down the wrong path.

Fix: keep the second attempt's DL_error message and include it in the Bus_connect_failed msg — 'libsystemd.so.0: <dl error>; libsystemd.so: <dl error>'. Keeping only the fallback's message is enough; keeping both is better.

title: gc: two catch-alls in opportunistic_sweep swallow Eio cancellation and Out_of_memory
description:
lib/gc/gc.ml:111-115 and 118-120. Pre-existing in shape; this diff moved the boot-id read inside the outer try and its new header comment now leans on the outer catch as a safety property ('opportunistic_sweep already wraps its body in warn-and-proceed, so there a raise degrades to a skipped sweep').

            | Schema.Unknown -> (
                try remove_project ~conn ~handle row
                with e ->
                  Printf.eprintf "pctl gc: warn — failed to sweep %s: %s\n" row.id (Printexc.to_string e))
      ...
      with e ->
        Printf.eprintf "pctl gc: warn — sweep aborted: %s\n" (Printexc.to_string e)

Warn-and-proceed is the documented policy for the sweep (gc.ml header: 'Failures warn to stderr and return unit; never abort the outer command'), and that policy is right for I/O failures. But 'with e' also catches Eio.Cancel.Cancelled, Out_of_memory and Stack_overflow. The cancellation case is user-visible: Ctrl-C during the sweep at the top of 'pctl up' prints 'pctl gc: warn — sweep aborted: Cancelled' and the command carries on into the rest of with_project instead of unwinding.

Fix: narrow both handlers to the failures the policy is about — Schema.Pctl_error, Sys_error, Unix.Unix_error — and let anything else propagate. Note the outer handler is also what the new header comment relies on to make a read_boot_id_exn raise degrade to a skipped sweep, so Sys_error must stay in the narrowed set.

title: test_helpers: write_temp_file never removes the file, leaking one temp file per test run
Session.reset bypasses the Clock port, so a frozen clock does not freeze the boot id that decides row deletion
description:
Introduced as a visible seam by the dead-code-cleanup diff (pctl-lrc), which made Clock the single boot-id source and added a 'clock' dependency to lib/state/dune.

lib/state/session.ml:55-57 calls the concrete reader directly:

  let reset (conn : Db.t) : unit =
    reset_with_boot_id conn ~boot_id:(Clock.read_boot_id_exn ())

while lib/cli/pipeline.ml:184 stamps the row through the port:

    let boot_id = P.Clock.read_boot_id () in
    ... session_id = (if boot_id = "" then None else Some boot_id);

Two consequences.

1. The Clock port is not honoured on the path that deletes rows. test/integration/test_pipeline_up.ml:25 uses 'Clock.frozen ~now:"2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00" ~boot:"test-boot"'. In that test with_connection (pipeline.ml:40-45) resets against the REAL /proc boot id while with_project stamps "test-boot", so reset_query's 'session_id != ?' predicate does not match what the test wrote. A second with_connection in the same test would NULL the row it just created. Today the tests do one pipeline call each, so it passes by luck.

2. The 'if boot_id = "" then None' branch at pipeline.ml:192 is dead in production and encodes a false invariant. Every path into with_project goes through with_connection first (pipeline.ml:169), where Session.reset already raised if the boot id was unreadable or blank. The site comment on Clock.Real.read_boot_id (clock.ml:53-56) presents "" as a legitimate NULL, but by the time it runs "" cannot occur. This is the same shape as the false 'single caller' comment the cleanup diff removed.

Fix (recommended): add read_boot_id_exn to Clock.S — Real forwards to the top-level function, frozen returns 'boot' and raises if it is empty. Have Pipeline.with_connection read it once through the port and pass it to State.Session.reset_with_boot_id, and reuse that same value for the with_project stamp. That honours the port on both paths, lets pipeline.ml:192's dead branch go, and drops the new 'clock' dependency from lib/state/dune since Session then only needs reset_with_boot_id.

Alternative, if the port should stay two-valued: leave Session.reset as-is and just delete the '= ""' branch with a comment naming with_connection as the guarantee. Cheaper, but leaves the frozen-clock inconsistency in (1).

comments.text: Seam is now committed as c7fb526033426ca04d980417e2d4b0d2419668d8. The comment on Clock.Real.read_boot_id was corrected in that commit to say "" is unreachable at Pipeline's stamp (with_connection runs Session.reset first) rather than presenting it as a legitimate NULL — point 2's false-invariant half. The port bypass itself is untouched and still owned here.

title: clock: the empty/unreadable boot id raises Sys_error, which pctl reports as 'unexpected error' with exit 1
description:
lib/clock/clock.ml:39, introduced by the dead-code-cleanup diff (pctl-lrc) on the prior review's own prescription ('raise Sys_error (boot_id_path ^ ": empty boot id")').

  if raw = "" then raise (Sys_error (path ^ ": empty boot id")) else raw

Sys_error is not Schema.Pctl_error, so it falls through to the catch-all in Cli.Pipeline.run (lib/cli/pipeline.ml:55-57):

  | e ->
      Printf.eprintf "pctl: unexpected error: %s\n" (Printexc.to_string e);
      1

The user sees 'pctl: unexpected error: Sys_error("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id: empty boot id")' and exit 1. The condition is expected, named, and diagnosable — reporting it as 'unexpected' with the generic bucket contradicts the exit-code taxonomy documented at lib/schema/schema.ml:486-497, where every known failure gets its own code.

Not urgent: the message does name the path and the problem, so it is debuggable. What is wrong is the channel.

Fix: raise Schema.Pctl_error with an arm that names the file and what to check. Registry_io { id; reason } fits without widening the error type (bucket 4). A dedicated arm is cleaner but changes the public error type and the exit-code table, which is a domain-model call.

Note for whoever takes this: test/unit/test_clock.ml asserts 'with Sys_error _', so the tests move with the change.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Introduced by c7fb526033426ca04d980417e2d4b0d2419668d8 as described. test/unit/test_clock.ml asserts 'with Sys_error _', so those four cases move with the fix.

title: e2e: daemon_reload intermittently fails with 'NoReply: Remote peer disconnected', failing the suite ~1 run in 3
description:
Observed during the review of the pctl-lrc working tree, on the host with a live user session ('systemctl --user is-system-running' -> degraded).

Measured this session:
  - dune build @e2e --force, run 1: exit 1
  - dune build @e2e --force, run 2: exit 0
  - dune build @e2e --force, run 3: exit 0
  - dune exec test/e2e/test_pctl_no_gc.exe, 6 solo runs: 6/6 exit 0

Run 1's failure, in test_pctl_no_gc at its first 'pctl up' (test/e2e/test_pctl_no_gc.ml:15, label up(a)):

  ASSERT up(a) exit=5
  ---- pctl stderr ----
  systemctl Reload - failed: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply: Remote peer disconnected

  Fatal error: exception Alcotest assertion failure

Exit 5 is the Bus_connect_failed / Unit_op_failed bucket (lib/schema/schema.ml:497). It came from Dbus.daemon_reload (lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:543-550) via check_rc.

Sequence-dependent, not test-local: the test passes 6/6 in isolation and failed only in the full suite, immediately after test_gc_explicit's 'pctl gc --yes' ('pctl gc: removed 1' / 'no projects registered' are the last lines before the failure). The suite runs the exes sequentially from one progn in test/e2e/dune:47-81, so this is a back-to-back Manager.Reload from a fresh connection right after the previous process's bus teardown.

'Remote peer disconnected' on a Reload call is the systemd user manager closing the connection while the call is in flight — a transient condition, not a pctl bug in the sense that the reload did not happen. pctl treats it as fatal.

Two things to decide, and they are separable:
  1. Should Dbus.daemon_reload retry a call that fails with NoReply / Remote peer disconnected (reconnecting the bus if needed) rather than surfacing exit 5? That is a product decision about pctl's robustness against a reloading user manager, not just a test fix.
  2. Regardless of (1), the e2e gate is currently ~2/3 reliable, so 'e2e green' is not a meaningful claim from a single run. Worth pinning down before anyone leans on it.

Not attributed to the cleanup diff: nothing in that diff changed the Reload call's semantics (call_method_no_args has the same ctypes signature as the deleted top-level sd_bus_call_method_no_args), and I did not run the suite on 0508423 to compare. Attribution is open.

title: UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md gc section describes a pre-SQLite state-dir design that no longer exists
description:
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:50-58 defines the gc vocabulary in terms of *state dirs* and *known markers*. Neither concept exists in the code: grep for state_dir/known_marker across lib bin test nix returns only an unrelated prose mention at lib/render/render.ml:115. Gc classifies rows in the SQLite 'projects' table (lib/gc/gc.ml:32-37), not directories under XDG_STATE_HOME, and there is no marker cross-referencing anywhere.

Every one of the three class rows contradicts Gc.class_of_row and Gc.purge:

- Doc 'Live: a state dir whose known marker points at a project path that still exists'. Code: Live iff session_id = current boot_id. Path existence is not the Live test.
- Doc 'Orphan: ... points at a project path that no longer exists'. Code: Orphan is the opposite — path EXISTS but there is no live session. Path-gone is Unknown.
- Doc 'Orphan ... the only class gc --yes deletes'. False: purge (gc.ml:120-133) matches 'Schema.Orphan | Schema.Unknown'.
- Doc 'Unknown: ... reported only, never deleted automatically'. False twice over: purge deletes Unknown, and opportunistic_sweep (gc.ml:93-112) deletes Unknown automatically on every mutating command (up/reload/down/restart).
- Doc line 50 'known markers written alongside the registry under lib/state/'. No such artifact.

This matters more than an ordinary stale comment: CLAUDE.md:11 instructs readers to read UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md *before writing code or docs*, so the wrong definitions are the first thing an agent or contributor absorbs — and 'Orphan means the path is gone' inverts the actual predicate that decides whether gc deletes a project's units.

Deliberately NOT fixed in the dead-code-cleanup pass: rewriting three domain-term definitions is a domain-model change, not a comment fix. Suggest driving it with the curu-domain-modeling skill so the replacement vocabulary (registry row / session id / boot id) is settled once and reflected in CLAUDE.md too.

Adjacent pointer-only staleness in the same file WAS fixed in that pass: :21 linked deleted lib/install/, :62 credited lib/plan/ with computing the diff (it lives in State.Projects.diff_manifest), :89-91 listed harness helpers and scratch fields that do not exist.
